notes: All table names are prefixed with doit_ because this project shares one Postgres database with other unrelated projects.

timeRules.timestampStorage: All instant-in-time columns are timestamptz (stored as UTC in Postgres).
timeRules.dateOnlyColumns: Period/deadline fields (start_date, end_date, due_date, period_start, period_end, prev_start_date, prev_end_date) are plain `date` columns with no time component.
timeRules.overdueRule: A task is overdue when: deleted_at IS NULL AND status != 'DONE' AND due_date < (today's calendar date in Asia/Seoul). A completed task is never overdue, even if due_date has passed.
timeRules.minutesRule: All durations (estimated_minutes, actual_minutes) are stored and aggregated as integer minutes in the database. Hour/minute display formatting happens only in the UI layer.

softDeleteRule: plans.deleted_at and tasks.deleted_at mark soft deletion. Every normal list query and every aggregation MUST filter deleted_at IS NULL. work_logs, completion_events, plan_revisions, and reflections have no deleted_at (they are immutable history/records and are cascade-deleted only if their parent row is hard-deleted, which this app never does).

completionDedupRule.description: Prevents duplicate completion under rapid/duplicate button clicks at the database level, not just in the UI.
mechanism: completeTaskAction runs inside a single DB transaction that SELECTs the task row FOR UPDATE, serializing concurrent completion attempts on the same task.
If the task is already status='DONE', no new completion_events row is created; the call returns an 'already done' result instead of an error.

Otherwise nextCycle = tasks.completion_cycle + 1, one completion_events row (task_id, nextCycle, idempotencyKey) is inserted, and tasks.status/completed_at/completion_cycle are updated -- in that order, inside the same transaction.

completion_events.idempotency_key UNIQUE and completion_events(task_id, completion_cycle) UNIQUE are the final backstop: if two transactions somehow still race past the row lock, the second INSERT raises a unique_violation (SQLSTATE 23505), which the application catches and treats as 'already done' rather than surfacing an error.

Uncompleting a task sets status='TODO' and completed_at=NULL. It never deletes or rewrites past completion_events rows and never touches completion_cycle. Re-completing afterwards consumes the next cycle number.

aggregationDefinitions.scope: A retrospective (`reflections`/'See' screen) is computed over a scope: either all non-deleted tasks of one plan, or all non-deleted tasks whose due_date falls within a chosen [start, end] range across plans.
aggregationDefinitions.plannedCount: count(scoped tasks where deleted_at IS NULL)
aggregationDefinitions.doneCount: count(scoped tasks where deleted_at IS NULL AND status = 'DONE') -- the CURRENT status count, not a count of completion_events rows.
aggregationDefinitions.overdueCount: count(scoped tasks where deleted_at IS NULL AND status != 'DONE' AND due_date < today_in_seoul)
aggregationDefinitions.blockedCount: count(DISTINCT task_id) among work_logs whose task is in scope AND blocker_reason IS NOT NULL AND trim(blocker_reason) != '' -- a unique-task count, NOT a count of work_log rows.
aggregationDefinitions.actualMinutesTotal: sum(work_logs.actual_minutes) for work_logs whose task is in scope
aggregationDefinitions.zeroFallback: Every aggregate defaults to 0 (never null/NaN) when the scope is empty.
aggregationDefinitions.evidenceDrilldown: Each aggregate is returned alongside the exact id list that produced it (plannedTaskIds, doneTaskIds, overdueTaskIds, blockedTaskIds, actualWorkLogIds) so the UI's evidence screen can render the underlying rows and re-derive the same total for verification.

topLevelFields: exportedAt (ISO-8601 UTC timestamp of when the export was generated)
exportFormat.excludes: Never includes SUPABASE_CONNECTION_KEY, SUPABASE_SECRET_KEY, SUPABASE_URL, or any other secret/connection value.

tables.name: doit_plans
tables.description: Top-level Plan unit of the Plan-Do-See cycle.
tables.softDelete: deleted_at IS NULL required in all normal list/aggregation queries.

tables.name: doit_plan_revisions
tables.description: Pre-edit snapshot of a plan, written every time the plan is revised. The plan's own id never changes across revisions.

tables.name: doit_tasks
tables.description: A to-do item belonging to a plan.
tables.softDelete: deleted_at IS NULL required in all normal list/aggregation queries.

tables.name: doit_work_logs
tables.description: An execution ('Do') record: an actual work session against a task. Never mutates plan/task estimates.

columns.name: end_at
columns.validation: end_at >= start_at, enforced in the server action before insert

columns.name: actual_minutes
columns.validation: = round((end_at - start_at) in minutes), computed server-side and persisted

tables.name: doit_completion_events
tables.description: One row per successful completion of a task's current completion cycle. Exists to make duplicate-completion prevention a database-level guarantee, not just an application/UI concern.

tables.name: doit_reflections
tables.description: A 'See' retrospective over a plan/period. carried_plan_id records which new plan this reflection's improvement was carried forward into.
